overview: Three despatches from American Consul Gerald Warner at Taihoku document a succession of destructive tropical storms affecting Japanese-ruled Taiwan and the Spratly Islands between August and December 1940. They describe the paths and wind speeds of the storms, damage to crops and infrastructure, flooding and loss of life, the sinking of the American yacht CYNJO at Keelung, and the devastation of the sparsely populated Spratly Islands by a typhoon and tidal wave. Together, the reports provide contemporary consular observations of disaster severity, economic losses, communications difficulties, and relief measures.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 117 on the typhoon of August 30, 1940
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, American Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports the meteorological, agricultural, infrastructural, and maritime damage caused by the August 30 typhoon in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Taihoku's worst typhoon in nine years, with peak winds of 40 m/s, damaged bananas, sugar, rice, cotton, tobacco, hemp, roads, and railways from Karenko to Keelung, sinking the American yacht CYNJO at its Keelung moorings.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 122 on the typhoon of September 29–30, 1940
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, American Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports extensive agricultural and property damage from Taiwan's third and worst typhoon of the 1940 season.
subfiles.summary: Warner reports Taiwan's worst typhoon in 26 years struck September 29-30 with peak winds near 48 m/s, destroying 10-20 percent of rice and sugar-cane crops plus property, with some loss of life, the season's third storm.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 130 on the Shinnan Gunto typhoon and tidal wave
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, American Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports the destruction and relief response following the December 5 typhoon and tidal wave in the Spratly Islands.
subfiles.summary: A December 5 typhoon and 18-foot tidal wave hit Shinnan Gunto, destroying all buildings, killing about eight, wounding dozens, and leaving roughly forty missing among 300 Japanese residents; delayed communications slowed relief shipments from Takao by a week.

interest: Shows three 1940 Taiwan-area typhoons' crop damage, flooding, and the sinking of an American yacht.
